ROOT_CAUSE:
The fix for this step was already committed, already tested and already green -- and could not run. `OPEN_BUILDING_UPGRADE` failed 10 times out of 10 on 2026-10-02, every one SEMANTIC_TARGET_NOT_VERIFIED carrying MAA_TEMPLATE:NO_MATCH:score=0.5146:gate=0.7/0.75, duration 0.171 s, empty after_screenshot. The runtime resolver reads the frame's own 升级 label and answers (0.4993, 0.7188) -- measured by the previous round and covered by tests/test_building_upgrade_entry_target.py. It was never asked: the routing file declared `preferred: MAA` with an autogen TEMPLATE node, and ExecutorRouter.execute iterates [preferred, fallback], while maa_resolver answers a miss with None and does not fall through. The no-fallthrough is deliberate and its docstring says why (a legacy resolver comparing a fixed ROI is position-blind, so a miss must not become a blind tap); the runtime resolver here is not position-blind, but nothing in the routing file said so.

Why the node could never answer, measured rather than inferred: its search window is x 335..483, y 288..432 (normalised y 0.225..0.338) while the frame's own OCR reads its 升级 token at (0.4993, 0.7188) = px (359, 920). Cropping both regions and looking at them settles it -- the window holds snow, a wall and a discarded plank; the control is a blue hexagon with a white curved arrow under the tutorial hand, which is exactly what the harvested template image shows. So the picture is right and the ROI is another frame's geometry, and this control is drawn wherever the selected building happens to sit, so no threshold adjustment explains the miss.
